checks.statement: A current PSMF exists, is located as notified and reflects the actual PV system.
Every PSMF change is recorded in the logbook with date, author and reason, and annexes are kept current with the main body.
The PSMF can be provided to an authority within 7 days of request, and a documented process defines who prepares and releases it.
The PSMF number and location held in the Article 57 database match the actual PSMF for every EU-authorised product.
PSMF annexes list all contracted PV service providers, SDEA partners and computerised systems in use, matching the current contract register.
An EU QPPV and deputy are appointed, reside and operate in the EU/EEA, and are available 24/7 with a documented back-up arrangement.
The QPPV has documented authority over the PV system and receives routine metrics on compliance, signals, audits and CAPAs.
A UK QPPV (or UK national contact person where required) is appointed and notified to the MHRA, with current contact details.
QPPV delegations to deputies and functions are written, signed and kept current, with no gaps during absences.
Local PV contacts are appointed in every market where one is required, trained, and overseen by the global PV function.
Every PV process, including intake, case processing, submission, signals, aggregate reports and RMPs, is covered by an approved, version-controlled SOP.
SOPs are reviewed at their scheduled interval and superseded versions are withdrawn from use and archived.
Local procedures and work instructions are consistent with global SOPs, and deviations from them are documented.
Each PV role has a defined training curriculum, and training on new or revised SOPs is completed before staff perform the task.
Staff outside PV who may receive safety information, including sales, medical and customer service, complete AE awareness training at hire and annually.
Training effectiveness is assessed and overdue training is escalated and tracked to completion.
A cross-functional safety governance body meets at a defined frequency and records benefit-risk decisions with rationale.
Senior management reviews PV system performance at least annually, including compliance KPIs, audit findings and resourcing.
There is a documented escalation route for urgent safety issues to the QPPV and senior management, with timelines.
All AE intake channels (phone, email, web, social media, MI, PSPs, partners) are inventoried and each is mapped to a documented route into the safety database.
Day zero is defined as first receipt of the minimum criteria by anyone in the company or its contractors, and is captured correctly in the safety database.
Serious unexpected cases are submitted within 15 calendar days, measured by source.
Company-sponsored websites and social media accounts are screened for AEs at a defined frequency, and screening is documented.
Solicited reports from organised data collection schemes are identified as solicited and processed per the applicable reporting rules.
Reports received by affiliates and local offices are forwarded to the global safety database within the SOP-defined timeline, and transfer timeliness is monitored.
Partner-received cases reach the safety database within agreed timelines; late cases are reconciled.
Case validity is assessed against the four minimum criteria, and invalid reports are retained and followed up where possible.
Seriousness, including medically important events, is assessed per ICH criteria with reference to an IME list, and downgrades require documented medical rationale.
Expectedness is assessed against the correct reference document version for each market (CCDS, SmPC, USPI or IB).
Medical review of serious cases is performed by qualified physicians or HCPs, with company causality recorded separately from the reporter's.
Events and products are coded with current MedDRA and WHODrug versions, and version upgrades are implemented within the release cycle.

checks.statement: Coding follows MedDRA Points to Consider and a company coding convention, with consistency checked in QC.

checks.statement: Narratives follow a template and contain the clinical course, treatment, outcome and relevant history needed for independent assessment.
A risk-based case QC program samples cases, trends error rates by field and processor, and feeds findings into retraining or CAPA.
Valid serious ICSRs are submitted to EudraVigilance within 15 days and non-serious within 90 days of day zero.
UK serious and non-serious ICSRs are submitted to the MHRA within 15 and 90 days respectively.
Follow-up information that is significant is submitted within the same 15-day timeline as the initial report.
Postmarketing 15-day reports for biological products, including vaccines, are submitted to FDA per 21 CFR 600.80.
A country reporting-rules matrix defines expedited and periodic ICSR requirements for every market where products are authorised, and is kept current.
Expedited reports in Japan and Canada meet local 15-day timelines and local reportability criteria.

checks.statement: Follow-up for serious and special-situation cases is attempted per a defined schedule with targeted questionnaires, and attempts are documented.
Pregnancy exposures are followed up to outcome, including infant status.
Follow-up requests do not breach data protection rules, and reporter contact details are handled per privacy requirements.
Duplicate detection runs on every incoming case using defined matching criteria, and confirmed duplicates are merged with a retained audit trail.
Duplicates flagged by EudraVigilance are investigated and resolved within the timelines requested.
At least weekly searches of a recognised database (e.g. Embase, Medline) cover every active substance the company holds, irrespective of brand.
For substances covered by the EMA MLM service, the MAH still screens literature outside MLM scope and reviews articles for non-ICSR safety information.
Literature cases meeting reporting criteria are submitted within 15 days of day zero, defined as the date a reviewer first identifies a valid case.
Articles are reviewed for safety findings beyond individual cases (e.g. signals, aggregate data) and relevant findings are passed to signal management.
Local journals not indexed in global databases are identified and screened in every market where products are authorised.
Local literature searches are performed at a documented frequency and results reach the global safety database within defined timelines.
The list of local journals is reviewed at least annually and updated for new market authorisations.
Search strings are documented, version-controlled and validated to retrieve known relevant articles.
Each search records date, database, string, hits and reviewer decision per article, retrievable for any past week.
Full-text articles are obtained promptly for potential cases, and translation of foreign-language articles does not delay day zero beyond reporting timelines.
Literature activities outsourced to a vendor have a vendor search QC and reconciliation of weekly outputs.
Signal detection covers all data sources (safety database, literature, clinical trials, EudraVigilance, partner data) at defined frequencies per product.
EudraVigilance data are monitored for all active substances at the frequency required, with eRMR review recorded.
Disproportionality thresholds and methods are documented and justified, and quantitative output is reviewed by a qualified person.
Periodic review of postmarketing safety data is documented per product, including for products with low case volumes.

checks.statement: Signal validation decisions are documented with the data reviewed, rationale and date, within defined timelines from detection.
Validated signals are prioritised by documented criteria (severity, public health impact, novelty) that drive assessment timelines.
Non-validated signals are retained with rationale and re-reviewed if new data emerge.
Validated signals are assessed using all relevant data, and assessments are completed within target timelines.
Signal outcomes are decided by a cross-functional body and translate into tracked actions (label change, RMP update, study).
Signal assessment conclusions are reflected in the next PSUR/PBRER and, where applicable, the RMP.
A single signal tracking system records every signal from detection to closure with dates and outcomes.
Emerging safety issues are notified to EMA and national authorities within 3 working days of awareness.
Validated signals from EudraVigilance monitoring are notified to the agency as required, as standalone notifications or via the PSUR.
Partners are informed of validated signals within timelines set in the SDEA.
PSURs/PBRERs follow the ICH E2C(R2) structure and contain an integrated benefit-risk evaluation, not only a data listing.
PSUR data come from validated, reproducible database outputs, and PRAC assessment requests are tracked to completion.
PADERs are submitted on schedule for every approved application, including unmarketed ones.
Quarterly PADERs are submitted within 30 days of quarter-end for the first 3 years, and annual PADERs within 60 days of the anniversary thereafter.
Any PADER waiver or PBRER substitution is supported by FDA agreement on file.
DSURs are prepared for every investigational product and submitted within 60 days of the DIBD anniversary.
DSURs include the RSI in effect at the start of the reporting period and a cumulative SAE summary.
US IND annual reports are submitted within 60 days of the IND anniversary.
A master schedule lists every periodic report with DLP, due date and owner, aligned to the EURD list and local requirements.
PSURs are submitted within 70 days of the DLP for intervals up to 12 months and within 90 days for longer intervals.
Late or missed periodic reports are recorded as deviations with root cause and CAPA.
Changes in EURD frequency or DLPs are checked monthly and the schedule updated.
An approved RMP exists for every product where required and reflects current safety concerns and pharmacovigilance activities.
RMPs are updated when new information may change the safety specification, and updates are submitted with relevant procedures.
Additional PV activities in the RMP, including imposed and agreed PASS, are on track against agreed milestones, and protocols and final reports are submitted on time.
ATMP risk management includes post-authorisation follow-up of efficacy and adverse reactions, with long-term follow-up of treated patients as agreed at authorisation.
Every approved REMS element is implemented as approved, with records showing each element is operating.
REMS assessments are submitted per the approved timetable (at minimum 18 months, 3 and 7 years post-approval).
REMS modifications are submitted to FDA before changes are implemented.
Approved aRMM materials (educational materials, patient cards, controlled access) are distributed in each market per nationally agreed key elements.
Local affiliates confirm aRMM implementation dates, and gaps are escalated to global PV.
aRMM materials are version-controlled and updated within agreed timelines after label changes.
Effectiveness of each aRMM is measured with defined process and outcome indicators, and results are reported in the PSUR/RMP.
Ineffective risk minimisation leads to documented corrective action.
The CCDS is maintained under a documented process with defined triggers and timelines for safety updates.
CCDS safety changes are approved by a labeling committee with documented medical rationale.
The CCDS version used for expectedness and PBRERs is clearly identified for every period.
Safety-related CCDS changes are submitted in every market within company target timelines, and delays are tracked.
US safety labeling changes are submitted per 21 CFR 314.70, including CBE supplements where appropriate.
Product information and patient leaflets in distribution reflect the latest approved safety text within agreed timelines.
Each IB contains a clearly identified RSI section, approved and version-controlled, used for SUSAR expectedness.
RSI changes take effect only after authority approval where required, and the version in force for each case is traceable.
A signed SDEA is in place with every partner that markets, distributes or develops company products.
SDEAs define exchange timelines, responsibilities for submissions, signals, PSURs and RMMs, and are reviewed at a defined frequency.
New partners have an SDEA signed before product launch or transfer.
SDEA commitments are tracked and partner non-compliance is escalated.
Vendors performing PV activities are overseen against KPIs and audited on a risk basis.
Contracts with PV vendors define tasks, KPIs, timelines, audit rights and data ownership.
Vendors are qualified before performing PV work, including assessment of systems and staff competence.
Vendor KPI breaches trigger documented corrective action and governance review.
Subcontracting by PV vendors requires company approval and is visible in the PSMF.
Safety data exchanged with each partner is reconciled at a defined frequency, and discrepancies are resolved and documented.
AE data from vendors (call centres, PSPs, market research) is reconciled with the safety database.
Reconciliation discrepancies are trended and recurring causes addressed through CAPA.
Partners are audited on a risk basis, with audit frequency justified by risk assessment.
Partner and vendor audit findings are followed through to CAPA closure.
Investigators report SAEs to the sponsor within 24 hours, and sponsor intake timeliness is monitored.
IND safety reports are submitted within 7 or 15 days as applicable.
Trial SAEs in the safety database are reconciled with the clinical database at defined intervals and before database lock.
SAE forms and processing conventions are consistent across studies.
Causality from both investigator and sponsor is captured for every SAE, and investigator causality is not downgraded.
SUSARs are reported in EU via CTIS/EudraVigilance within 7 days (fatal or life-threatening) or 15 days (other).
IND safety reports are distributed to all participating investigators.
Aggregate analyses of SAEs indicating important risk are reported as IND safety reports.
Ethics committees receive safety information as required by local regulation.
Blinded cases that qualify as SUSARs are unblinded by an independent person before submission, with the blind maintained for the study team.
Unblinding access is restricted and logged.
Unblinding is performed promptly enough to meet 7/15-day timelines.
A DMC charter defines safety review frequency, data flow and communication to the sponsor.
Safety content in protocols, IBs and informed consent forms is consistent and updated after RSI changes.
Safety signals from trials feed into DSURs and IB updates.
A single validated safety database is the system of record for all cases, and spreadsheet trackers are not used as a substitute.
Safety database configuration (reportability rules, product dictionary) is controlled and changes are tested before release.
Case records are retained for the required period after product withdrawal.
E2B(R3) gateway connections to each authority are tested and acknowledgements are reconciled.
Negative ACKs and failed transmissions are resolved and resubmitted within reporting timelines.
FDA electronic submissions via ESG are monitored for completion.
Data migrations are planned, validated with documented mapping and reconciliation, and no case data are lost or altered.
Post-migration verification confirms reportability and data integrity.
Computerised PV systems are validated per a risk-based approach with documented validation deliverables.
System changes follow change control, with impact assessment and regression testing.
Periodic review confirms systems remain in a validated state.
User access is role-based, granted on approval and reviewed periodically, with leavers removed promptly.
Audit trails capture who changed case data, when and why, and are reviewed.
A business continuity plan covering safety database outage is tested, including manual reporting fallback.
A risk-based PV audit strategy covers all PV processes, affiliates, partners and vendors over a defined cycle.
The annual PV audit plan is executed as planned, and deviations are justified.
Auditors are independent of the processes they audit and are qualified.
Audit and inspection findings have CAPAs with root cause analysis, owners and due dates.
CAPA effectiveness is verified before closure.
PV deviations, including late submissions, are recorded and assessed for impact.
Significant audit findings are communicated to the QPPV, and a note is placed in the PSMF.
Compliance KPIs for ICSR, PSUR and literature timeliness are measured monthly against targets.
KPI trends below target trigger investigation and CAPA.
Compliance metrics are included in the PSMF annex as required.
An inspection readiness plan with roles and a document request process is maintained and rehearsed.
Inspection findings are responded to within the deadline set by the authority, and commitments are tracked.
Inspection history and outcomes are recorded and inform the audit strategy.
Medical information enquiries are screened for AEs, and identified AEs are forwarded to PV within one business day.
MI and PV records are reconciled periodically to confirm no AE was missed.
MI staff are trained on AE and special situation identification.
Product complaints with an associated AE are forwarded to PV, and AEs with possible quality defects are forwarded to quality, within defined timelines.
Field Alert Reports are submitted within 3 working days when required.
Combination product postmarketing safety reports meet device and drug reporting requirements.
Safety-related regulatory commitments are tracked to completion.
Safety-related correspondence from authorities is routed to PV and answered within the requested timelines.
New information that could affect benefit-risk is communicated to authorities promptly.
Each patient support programme has a PV agreement and AE reporting process, with reconciliation.
Market research programmes have AE reporting obligations in contracts.
Digital channels and apps owned by the company are listed and screened for AEs.
AE reports from commercial programmes reach PV within defined timelines, with timeliness monitored.
